A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CATDiet/CombDiet study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support matching retained, revised and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition, corruption-robustness and depth-perception experiments in Figures 3–4, Table 1 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds curriculum, temporal-sampling, pairing, convergence and synthetic-object experiments.

M1.justification: The color and acuity curricula, adjacent-frame temporal objective, SimCLR/DINO adaptations and 30%/70% CombDiet phases remain unchanged. New schedule and pairing variants are experimental controls, not replacements for the proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds TOYS, a ten-class synthetic multiview subset of Toys4K, evaluated in Table S7. CO3D-50 and the corresponding ImageNet subsets already appeared in v1's appendix. Toys-200 is discussed but not reported as an evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: v2 adds PAPN and MADAug as evaluated curriculum-learning comparators for SimCLR-ResNet on CO3D-10 in Table S6. Existing diet-order controls, Non-Smooth, SHF and standard SSL comparisons are retained; the additional comparison is confined to one configuration.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated CO3D test sampling from two random frames per video to two frames at the training interval. New ablations vary stage durations at fixed total epochs, warm-up proportions, temporal stride and real-versus-warped frame pairing. The stated sampling revision does not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Section S2 tests stage-duration schedules, 30%/50%/70% warm-up ratios, halved/doubled temporal stride and two geometric-warping pairing alternatives. Section S5 adds convergence curves investigating whether the advantage persists after training stabilizes. These substantially expand checks of schedule sensitivity, temporal information and training sufficiency beyond v1's existing controls.

E5.justification: Table 1 and v1 Table S2, now Table S5, change from point estimates to mean ± SEM across three runs. New Table S8 reports mCE t-tests against STD. Figures 3 and S1 already reported three-run standard errors in v1, so this is an expansion of uncertainty reporting, without evidence establishing an increase in run counts.

E6.justification: Central tables and recognition plots contain revised results, alongside new ablation, comparator and TOYS outcomes. For example, Table 1's SimCLR-ViT CombDiet SAY accuracy changes from 55.1 to 54.5 ± 0.3. The CO3D-10-C SimCLR-ViT mCE ranking changes from CombDiet beating STD, 67.6 versus 68.6, to STD leading, 67.8 versus 68.0. Revised sampling and aggregation limit interpretation as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The blending expression, curriculum definitions and metric definitions remain substantively unchanged. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or revised in v2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions and discussion retain the same scientific claims: developmental visual diets improve robustness, produce biologically aligned patterns and benefit standard SSL through CombDiet. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining the principal contribution.

C2.justification: New Section S6 explicitly limits applicability to temporally coherent clips with a large central object and leaves unconstrained cluttered egocentric streams unresolved. New analyses interpret convergence as evidence against early-stopping effects and distinguish partial replacement by warped views from failure of single-view warping. v2 also qualifies some superiority statements, including changing the appendix's mCE advantage from all baselines to most cases.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promised future release with stated code, data and model availability and supplies a GitHub hyperlink. Section 4.2 clarifies that REV reverses stage-duration allocation as well as progression order. Existing optimizer, hardware and temperature-schedule disclosures remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify repository contents.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for PAPN, MADAug, synthetic-object datasets, Lu et al.'s developmental visual-diet work and attention-related future directions. The established positioning relative to developmental psychology, SSL and corruption robustness remains largely intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained, with localized wording edits, corrected table references, changed author order/contact information and an acknowledgement. The appendix inserts ablation, additional-analysis and limitations sections while retaining and renumbering the earlier supplementary sections.

P2.justification: v2 adds six supplementary tables, S2–S4 and S6–S8, and the two-panel convergence Figure S2. Existing result tables are reformatted to include SEM, recognition plots are updated, and v1 Table S2 becomes Table S5. This substantially expands the visual presentation of experimental evidence; Figures 1, 2 and 4 remain intact.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's point-estimate tables and narrower diagnostic evidence, v2 provides uncertainty estimates, targeted ablations, convergence checks and explicit applicability limits. These strengthen assessment of the existing claims. The gains remain bounded because adaptations of the added comparators and the sampling design of the t-tests are only briefly documented.
